newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates ease at mid-session.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates ease at mid-session.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates softened at mid-session on Monday on slightly easing liquidity in the banking system, dealers said.

At midday, the overnight interbank rate was at 6.351 percent against Saturday's 6.362 close -- still far outside the central bank's 5.00-5.5 percent target zone -- with 30-day commercial paper down to 6.35-6.40 against 6.40-6.45.

The money rates were likely to stay around the current levels, but dealers said money demand would gradually increase before Thursday's Labour Day holiday and the beginning of the routine monthly payroll period.
The bond market did not report any trade in the morning session.
The late morning announcement of Taiwan's index of leading business indicators, which rose for the seventh consecutive month in March, dampened buying interest, brokers said.
Investors feared that the indicators, which forecast peaks and troughs in the business cycle, showed Taiwan's economy is overheated.
